implementation_loop.description: Full Phase 0 -> Phase 1 loop. Corpus extraction and adapter serving run inside hex-nexus (the FS bridge / daemon); ACTUAL LoRA gradient training is offline dev tooling (scripts/train-lora.sh) because it is neither in-process Rust nor a daemon responsibility and would OOM a 16GB-GPU/30GB-RAM box (project_qwen_next_hardware_ceiling). Promotion authority is the bench gate, never training loss.
steps: 1. hex inference corpus build <expert>      -> .hex/corpus/<expert>/corpus.jsonl + manifest.json (auditable; every record carries source_path)
2. scripts/train-lora.sh <expert> [--run]   -> GGUF adapter (offline; rank 4 / alpha 16 / final-layer FFN per DMoE; requires HEX_LORA_TRAINER to actually train)
4. (serving) base+adapter rides the existing tier router automatically; absent/disabled/HEX_LORA_DISABLED -> bare base, never an error; touches NO correctness gate
5. hex inference adapter evaluate <expert>   -> bench gate: promote ONLY on first-draft acceptance lift with no quality/throughput regression; verdict stored as lesson:hex-lora-<expert>
implementation_loop.hardware_caveat: rank-4 LoRA on a 24-32B base is feasible but tight on 16GB GPU / 30GB RAM — prefer a quantized (q4) base or off-box training, and respect the resource governor (ADR-2606080915). The evaluate path requests governor admission and DEFERS (never OOMs) under memory pressure.
implementation_loop.invariant: ADR-2606161300 §1 HARD: removing every adapter must not weaken any correctness gate. The LoRA is an idiom prior, never enforcement.

specs.description: Building a corpus for a named expert produces human-auditable instruction artifacts on disk, derived only from hex's own ADRs/specs/exemplar diffs — never opaque/binary blobs.
specs.given: hex ADRs in docs/adrs/, behavioral specs in docs/specs/, and analyzer-passing exemplar source exist in the repo, and an expert name (e.g. hex-boundaries) maps to a declared knowledge-unit glob set.
specs.when: The operator runs `hex inference corpus build hex-boundaries` (CLI → nexus endpoint POST /api/inference/corpus/build).
specs.then: A corpus artifact is written under .hex/corpus/<expert>/corpus.jsonl as newline-delimited JSON instruction pairs (each {instruction, input, output, source_path, corpus_version}); every record carries the source_path it was derived from so a human can trace it back; and a manifest .hex/corpus/<expert>/manifest.json records the corpus_version, source globs, record count, and a content hash. No record lacks a source_path.

domain_conventions.augmentation: PRAG-style: per source artifact, one content-preserving paraphrase + N Q/A pairs; no answer-string leakage from benchmarks
domain_conventions.no_runtime_scripts: extraction runs in hex-nexus (the FS bridge), not a shell script

specs.description: Each expert's corpus is built only from its declared knowledge-unit globs; a source artifact outside the expert's unit never leaks into its corpus.
specs.given: hex-boundaries declares globs over docs/adrs/**/*hexagon*, CLAUDE.md hex rules, and analyzer-passing exemplars; hex-testing declares globs over docs/specs/** and Deps-pattern test exemplars.
specs.then: Every record in the hex-boundaries corpus has a source_path matching a hex-boundaries glob; no record is sourced from a hex-testing-only artifact. Building one expert never mutates another expert's corpus directory (decoupled units, DMoE-style).

domain_conventions.isolation: one corpus dir per expert; builds are independent

specs.description: A trained LoRA adapter is registered against a (base-model, tier, expert) tuple with a corpus-version stamp, and can be added/removed without touching the base model record.
specs.given: A LoRA adapter artifact (produced by the external training step) exists for the T2 qwen2.5-coder base, trained on the hex-boundaries corpus at a known corpus_version.
specs.when: The adapter is registered via `hex inference adapter register --expert hex-boundaries --base qwen2.5-coder:32b --tier 2 --artifact <path> --corpus-version <v>`.
specs.then: The registry persists an AdapterRecord {expert, base_model, tier, artifact_ref, corpus_version, enabled} ; the base-model endpoint record is unchanged; and `hex inference adapter list` shows the new adapter. Removing it (`adapter remove`) restores the un-adapted base path with zero change to any correctness gate.

domain_conventions.invariant: ADR-2606161300 §1 HARD: removing every adapter must not weaken any gate

specs.description: When an enabled adapter exists for the tier handling a request, the inference call serves base+adapter; otherwise it serves the bare base — selection is by the existing tier router, no new router.
specs.given: An enabled hex-boundaries adapter is registered for tier 2 on qwen2.5-coder, and a codegen task is routed to tier 2 by the existing strategy_hint tier router.
specs.when: hex-nexus issues the inference HTTP call for that task.
specs.then: The call targets the adapter-composed model (e.g. an Ollama model created with an ADAPTER directive, or the gateway passes the adapter ref) ; KV-cache reuse across the ReAct loop is preserved (adapter attached such that prefix cache stays valid) ; and if the adapter is disabled or absent, the identical request path serves the bare base with no error.

domain_conventions.routing: reuse existing tier router (strategy_hint); adapter rides the tier — no learned router
domain_conventions.serving_path: Ollama Modelfile ADAPTER directive for local GGUF LoRA, or inference-gateway adapter ref
domain_conventions.kv_cache: final-layer/attachment choice must not invalidate prefix cache (DMoE efficiency result)
domain_conventions.fallback: absent/disabled adapter → bare base, never an error

specs.description: BLOCKING: an adapter is only promoted to a tier default when the agentic bench suite shows first-draft acceptance-rate lift vs the bare base with no quality/throughput regression.
specs.given: A registered-but-not-default hex-boundaries adapter and the agentic inference benchmark suite (ADR-2606071734).
specs.when: `hex inference adapter evaluate hex-boundaries` runs the suite against bare-base and base+adapter on the same tier and tasks.
specs.then: The verdict records first-draft pass rate through `hex analyze` + the best-of-N compile gate for both; the adapter is marked promotable ONLY if (acceptance_rate_adapter > acceptance_rate_base) AND (general codegen quality_score not regressed beyond tolerance) AND (throughput tok/s not regressed beyond the configured budget). A non-lift or regressing adapter is NOT promoted, and the verdict is stored (`hex memory store lesson:hex-lora-<expert>`).

domain_conventions.verdict_authority: agentic bench harness (ADR-2606071734), NOT training loss
domain_conventions.primary_metric: first-draft acceptance rate through hex analyze + compile gate (ADR-2606072044)
domain_conventions.guard_metrics: no codegen-quality regression; no throughput regression beyond budget
domain_conventions.promotion: only on lift + no regression; else stays registered-not-default

specs.description: NEGATIVE: no correctness gate may be relaxed because an idiom adapter is active. Disabling every adapter must leave analyzer/spec/compile verdicts identical.
specs.given: An enabled hex-boundaries adapter serving tier-2 codegen.
specs.when: Generated code contains a hexagonal boundary violation (e.g. an adapter importing another adapter) that the model emitted confidently.
specs.then: `hex analyze` STILL flags the violation and the best-of-N compile/acceptance gate STILL rejects the draft exactly as it would with the bare base; the adapter never suppresses, bypasses, or pre-approves any gate; and removing all adapters yields byte-identical gate verdicts on the same input.

domain_conventions.principle: ADR-2606161300: LoRA = idiom prior, never enforcement; preserves independent-oracle property
domain_conventions.hard_invariant: gates are adapter-agnostic; token-uncertainty is NOT used as a rule oracle

specs.description: NEGATIVE: LoRA training/eval must request admission from the resource governor and be refused (not OOM-crash) when the 16GB-GPU/30GB-RAM box lacks headroom.
specs.given: The resource governor (ADR-2606080915) reports insufficient GPU/RAM headroom on the local box (per project_qwen_next_hardware_ceiling).
specs.when: An adapter training or evaluation job requests admission.
specs.then: The job is refused or queued by the governor with a logged reason; the daemon and other inference work are unaffected; no OOM crash occurs. Admission is required before any training/eval dispatch.

domain_conventions.constraint: project_qwen_next_hardware_ceiling: 16GB GPU / 30GB RAM — large-base LoRA may need quantized/off-box training

specs.description: When source ADRs/specs change (epoch or content), the corpus manifest content-hash changes, marking dependent adapters stale so they are not silently serving obsolete idioms.
specs.given: A registered adapter stamped with corpus_version V1, and an ADR in its knowledge unit is later edited (or the ADR epoch advances per ADR-2606071243).
specs.when: `hex inference corpus build <expert>` is re-run (or a staleness check runs).
specs.then: The new manifest content-hash differs from V1; `hex inference adapter list` flags the adapter as stale (registered corpus_version != current corpus_version); a stale adapter is surfaced for retrain and does NOT auto-promote.

domain_conventions.staleness: registered corpus_version != freshly-built manifest hash → stale
domain_conventions.epoch_link: ADR-2606071243 epochs as a retrain trigger
